lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.title: Launch and planning: professional email and message conventions

standardsRefs: Manuel Academy local Ready for Life composition
objective: I can complete a realistic professional email and message conventions task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.
scenario: The learner compares two provided fictional messages side by side, a casual text to a friend and a workplace email about the same underlying situation, names what changed between them, then drafts their own workplace message for a different fictional scenario using the same four-part structure.
safetyNotes: Both comparison messages are fictional and provided with this lesson; no real names, employers, or contact details are used.
materials: learner-local: the provided pair of fictional messages

tasks.directions: Analyze the complete worked example on swk-rfl-g10-u03-l01-model-card before beginning.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Complete the fictional coached case on swk-rfl-g10-u03-l01-guided-card, use criterion-specific feedback, and finish its fresh correction turn.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Choose the permitted real-life route or complete fictional route on swk-rfl-g10-u03-l01-independent-card; follow every step and retain only the named minimal evidence.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Complete the minimal evidence record on swk-rfl-g10-u03-l01-evidence-record; omit or fictionalize private details.

prompts.text: Which of the four parts do you think matters most for a workplace reader who is busy and skimming, and why?

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g10-u03-l01-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g10-u03-l01-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g10-u03-l01-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Comparison accuracy: Names at least two specific structural or wording differences. | Structural completeness of the draft: All four parts are present and identifiable. | Reasoning about audience: Names one part and a plausible reason tied to a busy, skimming reader. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g10-u03-l01-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Have the learner rewrite their draft as a very short chat-style workplace message (such as an internal messaging app) and explain which of the four conventions still apply and which relax in that format.

productionDepth.practicalGoal: I can complete a realistic professional email and message conventions task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.

duration.sessionPattern: 8–10 minutes model and planning, 8–10 minutes guided try, 20–30 minutes application, 7–10 minutes evidence and revision
duration.adultTime: No adult time required unless the learner chooses support

localMaterials.label: the provided pair of fictional messages

resources.title: professional email and message conventions worked model
resources.purpose: Shows the starting condition, visible moves, reasoning, and success check before the learner begins.
content: Starting condition: The learner compares two provided fictional messages side by side, a casual text to a friend and a workplace email about the same underlying situation, names what changed between them, then drafts their own workplace message for a different fictional scenario using the same four-part structure.
Model move 1: Read the condition and name the exact professional email and message conventions decision or action.
Model move 2: Read the casual text and the workplace email about the same situation, and list what's different between them.
Model move 3: Name the four structural parts of the workplace email: subject line, greeting, body, and closing.

Model check: Comparison accuracy: Names at least two specific structural or wording differences. | Structural completeness of the draft: All four parts are present and identifiable. | Reasoning about audience: Names one part and a plausible reason tied to a busy, skimming reader.

resources.title: professional email and message conventions action steps
resources.purpose: Provides the ordered directions used by the model, guided attempt, independent task, and retry.
content: 1. Read the goal, constraints, and privacy boundary for professional email and message conventions.
2. Analyze the worked model and identify why its sequence meets the criteria.
3. Complete the guided case and use feedback before moving on.
4. Select the permitted real-life route or the complete fictional route.
5. Carry out the task, retaining only the minimum evidence named in the record.
6. Compare the result with the success checks and complete the correction loop when needed.

resources.title: professional email and message conventions coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: The learner compares two provided fictional messages side by side, a casual text to a friend and a workplace email about the same underlying situation, names what changed between them, then drafts their own workplace message for a different fictional scenario using the same four-part structure.
Coach direction: Read the casual text and the workplace email about the same situation, and list what's different between them.
Learner prompt: List at least three specific differences between the two messages (beyond just 'one is more formal').
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: professional email and message conventions complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: Name the four structural parts of the workplace email: subject line, greeting, body, and closing.
Response 1 (t2-p1): I identified the subject line and what makes it specific rather than vague.
Response 2 (t2-p2): I identified the greeting, body, and closing and what each one does.
Equal-access rule: Use the fictional condition above and complete the same reasoning and evidence without private real-world details.

resources.title: professional email and message conventions minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.
Reflection: Which of the four parts do you think matters most for a workplace reader who is busy and skimming, and why?

Success checks: Comparison accuracy: Names at least two specific structural or wording differences. | Structural completeness of the draft: All four parts are present and identifiable. | Reasoning about audience: Names one part and a plausible reason tied to a busy, skimming reader.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: professional email and message conventions supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g10-u03-l01-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g10-u03-l01-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional professional email and message conventions condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.

Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — Comparison accuracy: Names at least two specific structural or wording differences. | Structural completeness of the draft: All four parts are present and identifiable. | Reasoning about audience: Names one part and a plausible reason tied to a busy, skimming reader..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g10-u03-l01-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

simulationRoute.title: professional email and message conventions — complete fictional route
simulationRoute.directions: Complete the professional email and message conventions task using the fictional condition and invented, non-sensitive details on the delivered independent card.
simulationRoute.completionCondition: Complete the same decision, procedure, evidence, and revision checks as the real-life route. No adult attests that a physical event occurred.

independentTask.privacyAlternative: The learner may use invented names, dates, amounts, organizations, spaces, and circumstances whenever real details are unnecessary or private.

retry.trigger: Start the correction loop when a required step is missing, the reason does not match the condition, a safety or privacy boundary is crossed, or the evidence does not show the stated result.
retry.targetedReteach: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g10-u03-l01-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step.

retry.feedback: Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments.
retry.parallelReattempt: Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g10-u03-l01-retry-pair without the coach prompt.

guardianInvolvement.role: Optional coach only; no guardian attestation is required.
guardianInvolvement.signOffBoundary: A guardian attestation certifies only that the named physical event occurred. It never scores the learner reflection or proves effort, honesty, maturity, responsibility, diagnosis, or character.

safety.stopRule: Stop the physical route when permission, supervision, a safe setting, or an expected material is missing, or when a new hazard appears. Continue only when the authorized adult resolves it; otherwise use the complete fictional route.
safety.physicalBoundary: The learner follows the source safety notes and never performs adult-only handling, transport, account, legal, medical, heat, sharp-tool, electrical, chemical, or machine actions.
safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.

privacy.rule: Collect the smallest process record that shows the lesson steps. A learner may choose fictional details and may decline private disclosure without losing credit.
doNotCollect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations
account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details
photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules

may: coach the guided and retry cards
mayNot: observe or claim a physical condition
tutorBoundary.physicalCompletionRule: Tutor or AI may coach. Tutor or AI may not certify that a real-world physical action occurred.
tutorBoundary.missingResourceAction: Stop and name the unresolved resource. Do not fabricate it; use another complete delivered route only when every resource for that route resolves.
